question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)

calls.reasoning: Recent NVIDIA next-quarter guides have been 1.115-1.155x the just-reported quarter (54/46.7, 65/57.0, 78/68.1, 91/81.6, 108/96.2). Q3 FY27 actual likely $111-114B given 12 straight beats of the high end (~3% above high end on average). That implies a Q4 guide of ~$124-131B. Management forecast 70% FY28 growth, supply is constrained and Rubin is ramping, all consistent with continued sequential growth. Downside: OpenAI run-rate miss jitters, memory constraints, and thin Polymarket markets on Q3 data center revenue that imply a softer Q3 (~$110B total). No market matches this contract; the Polymarket Q3 data center markets are near-misses with very low volume.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 (ended Jul 26 2026, PR Aug 26 2026): revenue $96.2B, +18% q/q, +106% y/y; Data Center $89.0B. Q3 FY27 guide $108.0B +/-2% (range $105.8-110.2B), no China DC compute assumed; GM 74.0% (nvidianews PR).
- Q1 FY27 (PR May 2026): revenue $81.6B; Q2 guide was $91.0B (actual $96.2B, +5.7% vs midpoint).
- Guide history (midpoints): Q1 FY26 43, Q2 FY26 45, Q3 FY26 54, Q4 FY26 65, Q1 FY27 ~78, Q2 FY27 91, Q3 FY27 108. Ratio of guide to the just-reported quarter: 54/46.7=1.156, 65/57.0=1.14, 78/68.1=1.145, 91/81.6=1.115, 108/96.2=1.123. Guide-to-guide increments: +9, +11, +13, +13, +17 ($B).
- Beat history: per Motley Fool Sep 15 2026, NVDA beat the HIGH end of guidance 12 straight quarters, actual averaging 3.1% above the high end over the last 4. Implied Q3 actual if repeated: ~$113-114B.
- Q3 consensus: ~$103.8B per one aggregator (likely stale, pre-guide); LSEG had expected a $104.2B guide before the $108B print.
- Aug 26 call: CFO forecast 70% y/y FY28 revenue growth (Street had ~44%); without supply bottlenecks it could exceed 100%. Supply constrained through FY28 (memory). Capacity commitments rose from $119B to $279B. Vera Rubin production started Aug 2026, ~1/5 of DC revenue in Q3. Amazon ordered 2M GPUs for 2027-28.
- GM guided to trough at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 (Rubin ramp), which signals heavy Q4 Rubin volume.
- Oct 16 2026: OpenAI disclosed a $50B run rate vs $68B expected; NVDA fell ~4% (Motley Fool). Demand-sentiment headwind; no change to NVDA guidance announced.
- Status quo: NVDA issues a +/-2% range around a midpoint; the question resolves on that midpoint rounded to $1B. Earnings date Nov 17 2026 after close.
- Resolves off the 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release (Q4 FY27 revenue midpoint), not the actual Q3 result or any later revision.
- Event window: the single publication on Nov 17 2026; as of Oct 17 2026, Q3 (ended ~Oct 25) is ~95% complete, and the release is 1 month away.
- Polymarket has thin markets (<$700 volume each) on Q3 Data Center revenue thresholds; no market on the Q4 guide was found.
- Searched for, not found: published consensus for Q4 FY27 revenue or for the Q4 guide; explicit management color on Q4 sequential growth.

calls.reasoning: NVIDIA's next-quarter guides have run 1.115-1.156x the quarter it just reported, recently ~1.12x, and guide-to-guide increments are +13, +13, +17B. Q3 FY27 actual is likely ~$111-113B: the 12-quarter streak of beating the high end points to ~$113B, while thin Polymarket Q3 Data Center markets point to ~$110B total. Applying ~1.13x gives ~$126B. The Rubin ramp, the Q4 gross-margin trough signalling heavy volume, and 70% FY28 growth support the step; supply limits, no China revenue and AI-demand sentiment (the OpenAI run-rate miss) cap it. No human market prices the Q4 guide; the Polymarket contracts are thin (<$700 volume) near-misses on Q3 Data Center revenue.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts (Q2 actual $96.2B, Q3 guide $108B, guide history, beat streak) and differed only in judgment: the size of the Q3 beat and which guide ratio to apply, giving medians of $125-128B. The thin Polymarket Q3 Data Center markets (>100B at 0.70, >105B at 0.25) imply total Q3 revenue near $110B, a bit below the beat-pattern ~$113B. I weighted them at ~$111-113B and applied ~1.13x, which supports a ~$126B median. The Q4 consensus figure ($124.5B vs ~$123B implied by FY consensus) and the report date (Nov 17 vs an unconfirmed Nov 25) cannot be settled without web access; neither changes the median materially, and the question resolves on the release whenever it comes out. Width carried from Runs 1 and 3 (~11).
